title: Chicago
logline: A hotel room in Chicago, 2001, from the back of a postcard that said 'the room is orange and I can hear the train.' Orange. A train drawn as sound in the window.

panels.composition: A hotel room drawn from six words: orange walls, a bed with the cover pulled tight, one window with the L-train drawn not as a train but as a smear of motion and a scrawl of sound across the glass. A postcard on the nightstand, picture side down. Nobody in the room. Never was, for him.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no panel borders, spare knowing ink line with economy, muted ochre and slate blue and sea-foam green washes, a small hotel room with orange walls and a tightly made bed, one window across which an elevated train is drawn as a smear of motion and scrawled sound rather than an object, a postcard face down on the nightstand, nobody in the room, no words
image.notes: Location id borrowed: the sequence's rooms are all 'elsewhere.' The room is invented from the 2001 postcard.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: 'The room is orange and I can hear the train.' Six words, one page.
